examples.en: The neighbor next door brought over some rice cakes.
I only exchange greetings with my neighbors.
Do you get along with your neighbors?
I returned the umbrella I borrowed from my neighbor.
At night I stay quiet out of consideration for my neighbors.
Our neighbor is a really kind person.

explain: 말할 때는 '이웃'이나 '이웃집 사람'이라고도 많이 해요. 아파트에서는 '옆집', '윗집', '아랫집'처럼 어디에 사는지 구체적으로 말하는 경우도 많아요.

phrases.en: The man next door and I are like family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가까이 살면서 정이 든 이웃을 사촌처럼 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Calls a neighbor you are close to a 'cousin' because you live so near and feel like family.

explain_en: In speech people often just say '이웃' or '이웃집 사람'. In apartment buildings people also often say '옆집' (next door), '윗집' (upstairs) or '아랫집' (downstairs) to be specific.

examples.en: I cut down on coffee this month.
I've cut back on how much rice I eat at dinner.

examples.ko: TV 소리가 너무 커요. 줄여 주세요.
examples.en: The TV is too loud. Please turn it down.
I want to cut down on salt. The soup is salty.

examples.ko: 이 사진은 너무 커요. 크기를 줄여요.
examples.en: This photo is too big. I'll make it smaller.

explain: 줄이다는 내가 줄이는 거예요. 저절로 작아지면 “줄다”예요: 옷이 줄었어요.

dict_examples.en: We downsized our home and moved.

explain_en: 줄이다 is something you do on purpose. When it shrinks by itself, use 줄다: 옷이 줄었어요 (“The clothes shrank”).

p.n: 감소시키다 is for abstract amounts, not turning down volume.

examples.en: I heard the president's remarks on the news.
Korea elects a president every five years.

examples.ko: 대통령은 오 년 동안 나라를 이끌어요.
examples.en: The president leads the country for five years.
The American president is coming to Seoul tomorrow.
I watched the president's speech on TV.

explain: 한국 대통령은 한 번만 할 수 있어요. 대통령 선거는 줄여서 “대선”이라고 불러요.

explain_en: A Korean president can serve only one term. The presidential election is shortened to 대선.

p.n: The speaker changes from the nation's leader to the head of a club or company.

examples.en: Let's go for a walk when the rain stops.
The baby wouldn't stop crying, and I was worried.
When the snow stops, let’s build a snowman together.
The shower stopped, so I folded my umbrella.

examples.ko: 비가 언제 그칠까요? — 저녁에는 그칠 것 같아요.
examples.en: When will the rain stop? — I think it will stop by evening.

explain: 비, 눈, 울음, 웃음처럼 계속되던 것이 멈출 때 써요. 자동차나 시계가 멈출 때는 ‘서다’, ‘멈추다’를 써요.

phrases.example: 그 가수의 인기는 그칠 줄 몰라요.
phrases.en: to show no sign of stopping (popularity, laughter, etc.)
phrases.nuance_ko: 인기·웃음·박수처럼 비가 아닌 것이 끝없이 이어질 때
phrases.nuance_en: used when something that is not rain, like popularity, laughter or applause, goes on endlessly
phrases.en_equiv: to show no sign of stopping (popularity, laughter, etc.)

explain_en: Use it when something that has been going on, such as rain, snow, crying or laughter, stops. For a car or clock stopping, use 서다 or 멈추다.

dis.h: rain, snow or crying comes to an end

p.n: The replacement sounds like the crying was halted, often abruptly. The original is a natural ending.

en: to neglect, to be lazy about

examples.en: The inspections were neglected, so the machine stopped.

examples.ko: 건강 관리를 게을리하면 나이가 들어서 고생해요.
examples.en: If you neglect your health, you will suffer when you get older.
I got lazy about exercising and my stamina dropped a lot.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 매일 연습을 게을리하지 않아요.
examples.en: That athlete never neglects practice, day after day.

examples.ko: 숙제를 게을리하는 학생에게는 보충 수업을 하겠습니다.
examples.en: We will give extra lessons to students who neglect their homework.

explain: '게으르다'는 성격이에요(게을러요). '게을리하다'는 해야 할 일을 열심히 하지 않는 행동이라서 '~을 게을리하다' 모양으로 쓰고, 붙여 써요.

dict_examples.ko: 일을 그렇게 게을리해서는 오늘 안에 못 한다.
dict_examples.en: If you slack off like that, you won't finish today.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: I neglected the housework, and now the house is a mess.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 게으르다 describes a nature (게을러요). 게을리하다 is the action of not putting effort into what you should do, used as ~을 게을리하다, and it is written as one word.

examples.en: I heard the survey results will be released next week.
I hear the price of the new product hasn't been announced yet.

examples.ko: 이 폴더는 공개 설정이라서 링크만 있으면 누구나 열 수 있어요.
examples.en: This folder is set to public, so anyone with the link can open it.

examples.ko: 박물관이 이번 주말에 유물 특별 공개 행사를 열어요.
examples.en: The museum is holding a special viewing event for relics this weekend.

examples.ko: 개인정보 공개를 막으려면 비밀번호를 자주 바꿔 주세요.
examples.en: To prevent your personal information from being exposed, please change your password often.

explain: '공개'는 숨기지 않고 모두에게 보이거나 알리는 거예요. 반대말은 '비공개'예요. SNS에서는 '전체 공개', '친구 공개', '비공개'로 누가 볼 수 있는지 정해요.

explain_en: 공개 is making something visible or known to everyone without hiding it. The opposite is 비공개. On social media you choose who can see a post: 전체 공개 (public), 친구 공개 (friends), 비공개 (private).

examples.ko: 세대별로 보면 소비 방식이 크게 다르다.
examples.en: By generation, consumption styles differ greatly.

examples.ko: 세대별 선호 브랜드를 비교한 결과를 보고드리겠습니다.
examples.en: I will report the results of comparing preferred brands by generation.

examples.ko: 명절 풍경도 세대별로 많이 달라서 이야기하다 보면 재미있어요.
examples.en: Even the holiday scene differs a lot by generation, so it's fun to talk about.

examples.ko: 세대별 연금 수령액 격차를 줄이는 방안이 논의되고 있다.
examples.en: Ways to narrow the gap in pension payouts between generations are being discussed.

examples.ko: 설문 결과를 세대별로 나눌까요? — 네, 부모 세대와 자녀 세대로 나눠 주세요.
examples.en: Shall we divide the survey results by generation? — Yes, split them into the parents' and the children's generations.

explain: '세대'는 같은 시기에 태어나 비슷한 경험을 한 사람들이에요. 그래서 '세대별'은 나이 숫자보다 'MZ세대'처럼 시대 경험이 비슷한 묶음을 비교할 때 써요.

dict_examples.ko: 직장인들은 세대별로 야근에 대한 인식 차이가 뚜렷한 것으로 나타났다.
dict_examples.en: Office workers' views on overtime were found to differ clearly by generation.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 세대별로도 뚜렷한 차이를 보여 아침 일찍 투표소를 찾은 투표자 대부분은 중·장년층이었다.
dict_examples.en: There was also a clear difference by generation: most voters who came to the polling stations early in the morning were middle-aged or older.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: A 세대 is a group born around the same time with similar experiences. So 세대별 compares groups like the 'MZ generation' rather than plain age numbers.
